text: The initiative features an end-to-end early warning system design focused on drought, integrating upstream observations, forecasting, and downstream advisory delivery. It extends forecast lead times from 24 hours to up to 7 days, significantly improving preparedness windows. The project also emphasizes subseasonal-to-seasonal prediction capacity, crucial for drought monitoring and anticipatory action. Strong regional technical partnerships with organizations like the Australian Bureau of Meteorology facilitate the transfer of methods and operational know-how tailored to PNG’s needs.

metadata.solution_name: CREWS–Papua New Guinea: Weather and Climate Early Warning System (CREWS–PNG)
